Shared witness and honest confession make fellowship more than a claim

Verse 5 gives the message: God is light. Verses 6–10 are five sentences that each begin with “if.” Verse 6 rejects a claim of fellowship made by one who walks in darkness. Verse 7 gives the true case, with two results. Those who walk in the light have fellowship with one another. The blood of Jesus also cleanses them from all sin. So walking in the light does not mean having no sin (verses 8–9).
Remaining in the received message requires love amid denial and departure

Verse 9 tests a claim to be in the light while hating a brother. The verse says he is still in darkness. Verse 10 gives the opposite case. One who loves his brother remains in the light. Nothing in him causes stumbling. Verse 11 says the hater walks in darkness and cannot see his way. So light and darkness are told apart by conduct toward a brother.
Love takes visible form through shared goods rather than claims of belonging alone

Verse 16 defines love by an act: Christ laid down his life for us. Verse 17 brings it down to an ordinary case. Someone has the world’s goods and sees a brother in need. If he closes his heart, how does God’s love remain in him? Verse 18 draws the rule. Love is not in word or tongue only; it is in deed and truth. Verse 19 says this is how they know they are of the truth.
Confession and visible love test claims about the unseen God

Verse 12 says no one has seen God at any time. That makes a claim to love God hard to check. Verse 20 supplies the check. A brother can be seen. One who does not love a seen brother cannot love the unseen God. A man who says he loves God and hates his brother lies. Verse 21 makes it a command: love God, and love a brother also.
Shared testimony supports confidence while prayer remains directed by God's will

Verse 13 gives the writer’s purpose: that believers know they have eternal life. Verse 14 names what follows from that knowledge: boldness toward God. The boldness is about prayer. The verse sets one condition: asking “according to his will.” Under that condition, he listens. Verse 15 adds that if he listens, they have what they asked. Verse 16 gives a first use: asking life for a brother who sins.
